chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Hasan ibn Atiyya, who said:

Sulayman ibn Khalid asked him (peace be upon him) and I was with him, about a man who circumambulated the House six circuits. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'And how does he circumambulate six circuits?' He said: 'He faced the Stone and said, "Allah is the Greatest," and he committed to one (circuit). So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'He should circumambulate one circuit.' He said: 'Supposing he loses it until he goes back to his family?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should instruct someone to circumambulate on his behalf.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone makes a mistake in counting their Tawaf circuits?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling for a pilgrim who mistakenly counts six circuits instead of seven by completing the seventh, illustrating the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in ritual acts. The Imam further permits sending a proxy (*na'ib*) to complete the missing circuit if the pilgrim is unable to do so personally, highlighting the flexibility within Shia jurisprudence for resolving ritual errors (*khata*).

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Hassan Bin Atiyya who said,

‘Suleyman Bin Khalid asked himasws and I was with him, about a man who performs Tawaaf six circuits by the House (Kaaba). Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘And how come he circumambulated six circuits?’ He said, ‘He kissed the (Black) Stone and said, ‘Allahazwj is the Greatest!’, and he committed to the one’. So Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘He should circumambulate one circuit’. He said, ‘Supposing he loses it until he goes back to his family?’ Heasws said: ‘He should instruct someone to do Tawaaf on his behalf’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from al-Hassan ibn ‘Atiyyah who has said the following:

“Sulayman ibn Khalid asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when I was there, about a man who performed six times Tawaf (walking around the House). Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, asked, ‘How did he do so? He said, ‘He faced the Black Stone and said, “Takhir (Allah is great beyond description),” made his intention and made it one.’ Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘He makes one time walking around the House?’ Sulayman said, ‘He missed it until he came to his family.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He must appoint someone to perform Tawaf on his behalf.’”
